_startNote: DECISIONS D14. These encode Sakhile being local rather than an outside developer. He opens high with the people who knew his grandfather and low with the institutions that lend money — an outside developer would have exactly the opposite problem, and a much bigger cheque. The low opening cash is the point: the first act is about getting funded, and the two ways to get funded (Renier fast and expensive, Amara slow and cheap) are the first real choice in the game.
_burnNote: Sakhile runs lean because he is local — no Sandton office, no consultants on retainer. That is both realistic and the mechanical expression of D12: his overhead is low, but so is his capital, so the paper years are survivable only if he gets funded before they end.
